incoming.name: Ancient Egypt
incoming.excerpt: Beginning from around 2700 BC, Egyptians used pictograms to represent vocal sounds -- both vowel and consonant vocalizations (see Hieroglyph: Script).

incoming.name: Isis
incoming.excerpt: However the true Egyptian pronunciation remains uncertain because their writing system omitted vowels.

incoming.name: Korea
incoming.excerpt: Each block consists of at least two of the 24 Hangul letters ( jamo): at least one each of the 14 consonants and 10 vowels.

incoming.name: Osiris
incoming.excerpt: The name was first recorded in Egyptian hieroglyphs only as ws-ir or os-ir because the Egyptian writing system omitted vowels.

incoming.name: Isle of Wight
incoming.excerpt: …dropping of some consonants and an emphasis on longer vowels.
